evidence.detail: Native read of the approved ASM projection shows bytes 31 C0 C3 at stated EA 0x1000: xor eax, eax; ret (lines 2–4). The XOR clears all 32 bits of EAX; the near RET pops the return address without immediate argument cleanup. SHA-256 is controller-reported, not worker-computed. SYNTHETIC opcode evidence only; not an IDA/FF8 native gate.

propositions.text: In this synthetic x86-32 fixture, normal execution returns with EAX=0 (also AX=0 and AL=0). XOR sets ZF=PF=1, clears CF=OF=SF, and leaves AF undefined; RET preserves those flags, loads EIP from [ESP], and advances ESP by four bytes. No arguments are accessed, callees invoked, or data memory written. Under an EAX-return ABI the return value is zero; the sequence alone does not establish cdecl, argument count, or a source-language return type.
